sentences.text: The single known specimen of this animal measures more than one meter from the tip of the skull to the base of the tail.
It is distinguished by unique skull features, including a nasal bone with a dorsal midline crest and a frontal ridge reaching the midline between the prefrontals.
The lower jaw has outer sculpture limited to the dentary bone and lacks a peg on the occipital surface of the mandibular symphysis.
The skeleton preserves the remains of an unidentified sphagesaurid crocodyliform inside its abdominal cavity.
The fossil remains were discovered in the Buruti creek area of the General Salgado municipality in southern Brazil.
Aplestosuchus was a fully terrestrial predator, similar to other baurusuchids.
Aplestosuchus is classified within the family Baurusuchidae, alongside other genera like Campinasuchus and Gondwanasuchus.
The parent group of the genus Aplestosuchus is Baurusuchinae.
Aplestosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Aplestosuchus is Aplestosuchus sordidus.
Aplestosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 93.5 to 83.5 million years ago.
Other estimates place its existence during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
The genus name Aplestosuchus combines the Greek word for "insatiate" or "gluttonous" with the name of the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
The species name sordidus means "filthy" and refers to the animal's greedy predatory behavior.
